CoherentModes · explore/mamba_contexts (v2)

Coherent sets over token contexts in mamba-130m

A follow-up to the v1 Mamba coherent-sets study: what v1 was looking at, and what the same construction finds when the items are token contexts.

MEASURED · 1 model · 2 checkpoints
Model, items and views

The question. The first Mamba study ("v1", explore/mamba_coherent/) found little in mamba-130m: its headline sets recovered the five document sources, which a bag of tokens also recovers, and almost none of its zoom cuts read as a clear split. Were we looking at the wrong things?

The answer: partly

v1 missed token-level organisation, because it scored its sets mainly against document source. The follow-up (v2) makes that organisation visible. It does not find clear clusters, and it finds no source grouping stronger than a bag-of-tokens reference gives. Three of the seven pre-registered targets failed.

  • Two separate problems in v1.
    • It scored the wrong labels. Its "depth blocks" (one position, read across layers) group contexts by the kind of token just read (newlines, function words, punctuation, LaTeX), but v1 scored them only against source.
    • There were no clear clusters to recover. Its spectra have no strong gap, and changing the labels would not have created one.
  • v2's items are single token contexts: 8,000 prefixes, each ending at a sampled token. Their coherent sets are scored against the token, the next token, the snippet and the model's own predictions.
  • The residual stream groups contexts by the class of the token just read. Agreement with that class is 0.49 on a 0 (chance) to 1 scale, against 0.16 with source. On top of that there is a small association with what the model predicts next, beyond what sharing the token explains. These groupings fade within one or two tokens of further reading.
  • The recurrent state groups contexts by source (agreement 0.73), and its groupings mostly last at least sixteen tokens.
    • A plain bag of the prefix's tokens groups by source just as strongly, so this probe cannot show that the state tracks the document beyond its vocabulary.
    • The state also carries the token-class and predictive associations, which the bag does not.
  • Not found.
    • No object is certified as clustered at the tested numbers of parts. The residual block is excluded under the θ = 3 rule; the state blocks leave some cases undetermined (not evidence either way).
    • The whole state keeps more of its walk within a snippet than the residual block does (excess share 0.22 against 0.03), but the gap is below the 0.2 the target required (K2).
    • Predictive coherence does not rise by the predicted amount from layer 4 to layer 24 (K3).

Targets met: K1, K1b, K4, K6; not met: K2, K3, K5; every control passes. Read on: Findings (claims, evidence, alternatives), Explorer (the sets themselves), Measurements (one figure per question).

The diagnosis of v1 in detail

v1 had two kinds of block, and the diagnosis concerns both. A reading block follows one layer along a snippet (positions 4..128) and averages the walks; a depth block takes one position and averages across layers L4..L24. AMI below is the agreement between a block's hard sets and a labelling (0 = chance, 1 = identical); r is the number of sets.

  1. Reading blocks were scored against source, and recover it the way a bag of tokens does. Averaging along a snippet keeps what persists along a document, which on that probe is its vocabulary. The 18 reading blocks' sets agree with source at AMI 0.46 to 0.86, and a bag-of-tokens reference finds the same partition.
  2. Depth blocks group by the kind of token just read, which v1 never scored.
    • Their sets agree with the current token's class at mean AMI 0.35/0.41/0.46/0.47/0.47 for r = 2/3/4/6/8, against 0.14/0.12/0.13/0.14/0.15 with source.
    • The class signal holds within one source (AMI 0.32 to 0.48), while source within one class is weak (0.08 to 0.15).
    • 16 of the 48 depth-block sets at r = 8 are at least 70% one class: function words, line ends, punctuation, LaTeX. The rest are mixtures or broad word buckets.
  3. Separately, there were no clear clusters to recover.
    • v1 called a cut "clear" when its two-way ratio Υ reached 3. 1 of 28 cuts did, and 22 fell within 2% of an even split, which is what a cut with no bottleneck does.
    • Asking for more parts does not help. At v1's two block roots, the multi-way ratio $\hat\Upsilon(k)$ for k = 2 to 8 parts is 1.09 to 1.36 and 1.00 to 1.58, against the same threshold of 3. Even the partition into the five sources scores only 1.16 and 1.18.
    • The spectral cap $2\mu_k/\mu_{k-1}$, which no partition can exceed, is 2.03 to 2.85 and 2.08 to 3.58. Where it is above 3 (T4 at k = 2, 4; T1 at no k) a clear partition is possible in principle, but none of the tested ones reaches it, and the spectra show no large gap at any k.
  4. The walk merges two of the five sources. In v1's whole-state snapshot the walk crosses between code and forum more often than chance (mixing ratio 1.36, where 1 means no avoidance and the null band tops out at 1.06). Every other pair is avoided (at most 0.37). This describes how the model treats the texts, not a flaw in the probe's design; it means source is a roughly four-group labelling.

The figure is the short version (full version: Measurements, F1; details in explore/mamba_coherent/diagnosis/DIAG_NOTES.md).

What v2 looks at instead

  • Items. A token context is the prefix of a v1 snippet ending at a sampled token t: 8 positions in each of 1,000 snippets, t = 16..112, N = 8,000.
  • Views at every layer (diagram above):
    • the residual after each block (point);
    • each layer's recurrent state (state);
    • the whole state.
    The headline block, B-point, is the residual across L1..L24; B-state does the same for the states. Reading is measured by re-reading the same items τ = 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 tokens later.
  • Groupings to score against.
    • Label-free: the token at t, the token at t+1, the snippet.
    • The model's own outputs: its top prediction, and predictive coherence, which is how similar the next-token distributions of contexts the walk links are. Its conditional form asks the same beyond what sharing the token explains.
    • For validation only: source and a 12-class token taxonomy.
  • References that use no model state at all: a bag of the prefix's tokens, the last 16 tokens, and the model's next-token distribution. They show how much of a grouping plain token statistics already give.
  • Readouts that need no clusters: walk shares, η² of each eigenfunction, retention along reading, span agreement. There is also a multi-way clustering certificate with three outcomes (certified, excluded, undetermined). The formulas are in Method.

Where each question is answered

  1. What the residual's depth sets group: the class of the token just read, plus a small predictive part beyond the token (Findings 1–2, Measurements F2 and F4).
  2. What the state's sets group: source, matched by the bag reference for source but not for token class or prediction (Finding 3, F2 and F4).
  3. How long sets last along reading: residual sets about one or two tokens; state sets mostly beyond sixteen, with one fast-fading exception (Finding 4, F5).
  4. Clear multi-way structure: not certified anywhere; excluded under the θ rule for the residual, with undetermined cases left for the state (Finding 5, F3 and F6).
Experiment map

The model is the released mamba-130m and its HF random initialisation; nothing is trained here, so there are no training curves.

Verdict against SPEC section 7

4 of 7 hypotheses met (K1, K1b, K4, K6); not met: K2, K3, K5. Controls and gate: 10 of 10 pass; not run: none; failed: none. The largest Sinkhorn row error, 1.93e-12, passes the 2e-12 gate narrowly.

Key. κ: the walk's predictive coherence (walk-weighted similarity of the model's next-token distributions); κ̃: κ above chance; κ̃|T: above what sharing the token at t gives. T̃, Ũ, W̃, C̃_c: how much more often than chance the walk stays within the same token, snippet, source or token class (0 = chance, 1 = always). AMI: agreement between hard sets and a labelling (0 = chance, 1 = identical). τ: tokens read after t. R: the tested numbers of parts {2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32}. Whole cell: the whole-state snapshot. Retention: how much of a set vector the later walk keeps (1 = all, about 0 = chance).

Statuses are recomputed here from the values in targets.json and validation.json (a mismatch with the stored flag is printed by the build). K1 compares two AMIs and has no null; read it with K1b.

These are readings of one model (mamba-130m-hf), two checkpoints and one probe of 8,000 token contexts from 1,000 snippets. Each finding opens with a claim and a tag: observed (read directly off a figure), reading (an interpretation of observations), speculation, or not determinable. Then come the evidence and what else it could be. Set numbers refer to the r = 8 set cards in the Explorer. Source and token class are validation labels; nothing here enters THEORY.md.

Scales used below: AMI is the agreement between hard sets and a labelling (0 = chance, 1 = identical). A share with a tilde (T̃, C̃c, W̃, Ũ) is how much more often than chance the walk stays within the same token, token class, source or snippet (0 = chance, 1 = always). Span agreement a₈ is the overlap of two objects' leading eight eigenfunctions (chance about 0.001, 1 = the same span). Retention is how much of a set vector the walk keeps (about 0 = chance, 1 = all).

1. The residual's depth sets group contexts by the class of the token just read, with a small predictive part beyond the token

Claim (observed). At r = 8, B-point (the residual across L1..L24) has eight hard sets. 786 of the 8,000 items are left unassigned and are excluded from the set descriptions and AMIs below. Of the groupings scored, the sets agree most with the class of the token at t:

  • AMI 0.49 with the class at t;
  • 0.20 with the class at t+1, 0.19 with the token id at t, 0.16 with the model's top-1 prediction, 0.16 with source and 0.12 with the next token. K1 is met.

5 of 8 sets are at least 70% one class. Several sets span many token identities (in the median set the commonest token is 0.23 of the set's items, and 84 distinct tokens make up 90% of them). Others are dominated by one newline or punctuation token. The strongest measured association is with the chosen token-class taxonomy. Since a class is a coarsening of the token id, that ordering alone does not show organisation beyond token identity. The ordering is unchanged with 8 or 30 graph neighbours instead of 15 (AMI with the class 0.50 and 0.52).

The sets, read from the cards (observed; "class" and "source" give each set's make-up).

  • Set 1 (164 items): line ends in verse. The token at t is '↵', '_', '␣_', '␣␣' (class make-up newline 89%, symbol 9%; source make-up poetry 98%, wiki 2%), followed by 'And', 'I', 'The', 'So'.
  • Set 2 (355): LaTeX inside maths text, such as the subscript in $H_x$ (class latex 40%, symbol 17%; source maths 85%, forum 10%).
  • Set 5 (201): sentence-final '.', '?', '$.', ':' across sources (class sentence punct 83%, latex 7%; source maths 29%, wiki 27%).
  • Set 7 (245): commas at the end of a verse line (class sentence punct 90%, symbol 7%; source poetry 76%, forum 13%).
  • Set 4 (510): pronouns and auxiliaries ('␣to', '␣I', '␣it', '␣you'; source poetry 43%, forum 35%).
  • Set 8 (1,605): articles and prepositions ('␣the', '␣of', ',', '␣in'), followed by '␣the', '␣a', '␣$', '␣in'.
  • Set 6 (1,073): code layout, with newlines and indents (source code 54%, forum 29%).
  • Set 3 (3,061 items; 1,768 distinct tokens make up 90% of it): everything else, mostly word pieces and numbers.

This is v1's depth-set picture again (Overview, diagnosis point 2), now on token contexts. Two of the sets (1 and 7) are a class within one source.

Beyond the token (observed).

  • The walk's predictive coherence κ is the walk-weighted similarity of the model's next-token distributions across the pairs of items it links, here 0.299.
  • When the predictions are shuffled among items that share the token at t, κ falls to 0.203 (band 0.201 to 0.204).
  • The remaining association beyond the token, κ̃|T = 0.12 (on the excess scale, 0 = what the token alone gives), is well above its null (-0.001 to 0.002). K1b is met.

η² of the modes (the share of an eigenfunction's variance between groups, λ-weighted over ψ₁..ψ₁₆) is 0.27 for the class at t (chance 0.001) and 0.06 for source. The token-level η² values look larger (0.67 for the token, 0.57 for the next token), but with thousands of groups their chance levels are high (0.412 and 0.403), and the bag of tokens reaches 0.45 for the token. Read those against their chance, not against η² for class.

How I read it (reading). The residual's coherent sets say what kind of token was just read. There is a real but small component of contexts that predict alike beyond their token. The evidence does not support calling them prediction classes: the sets agree with the model's prediction (AMI 0.16) far less than with the current class, and the pred reference's own sets agree with B-point's only at AMI 0.35.

What else it could be.

  • The classes are a function of the token, so a high class score partly restates token identity at a coarser grain.
  • The regular-expression taxonomy is one choice; the set cards show the tokens themselves.
  • The cause of κ̃|T is open. Context features that vary with the token's surroundings (the same token in verse or in code) can both bring items together in the walk and change their predictions. The walk need not be grouping contexts because they predict alike.
  • 30% of items have a token unique in the probe and keep their own prediction under the null, which makes the null conservative.

2. Up the residual stack, token identity fades and source grouping rises; predictive coherence peaks before L24

Claim (observed). Shares in the point snapshots (F2), trained:

  • the token at t falls from 0.38 at L4 to 0.10 at L24;
  • the class at t falls from 0.78 to 0.37;
  • source rises from 0.41 to 0.68 (largest 0.73 at L22);
  • κ̃ goes from 0.19 to 0.26, with its largest value 0.35 at L21;
  • κ̃|T goes from 0.06 to 0.16 (largest 0.22 at L21).

K3 is not met. T̃ is higher at L4 than at L24, as predicted, but κ̃ rises by less than the 0.1 the target asks for (0.19 to 0.26). The depth thirds' sets shift accordingly:

  • the late third's (L17–24) agree with source (AMI 0.42) more than with the class (0.25);
  • the early third's follow the class (0.58);
  • the early and late thirds agree with each other only at AMI 0.20.

How I read it (reading). Along depth, the residual's grouping moves away from the current token and towards the two proxies measured here, source and predictive coherence. The target was written for L24; on these data predictive coherence peaks a few layers earlier and falls back at the last layer. That is an observation about where the peak sits, and it does not turn K3 into a pass.

What else it could be. Rising W̃ need not mean the residual represents the document, because local vocabulary already separates sources. The recent reference (mean embedding of the last 16 tokens) has W̃ 0.60, and the bag reference 0.87. A residual that mixes in recent context would show the same rise.

3. The recurrent state's sets are source sets; a bag of tokens matches that source grouping but not the state's class and predictive associations; K2 is not met

Claim (observed). On the hard sets (AMI):

  • The whole state's r = 8 sets agree with source at AMI 0.73, and with the class at t only at 0.15.
  • B-state's (the per-layer states across depth) agree with source at 0.74.
  • B-state and the whole state agree with each other (AMI 0.93; span agreement a₈ 0.86).
  • Both barely agree with the residual (B-point against the whole state: AMI 0.25, a₈ 0.26).

On the walk shares:

  • the whole state's snippet share is Ũ = 0.22, against 0.03 for B-point. The target asked for at least 0.2 more, so K2 is not met, although its first half (AMI with source above AMI with class) holds;
  • the per-layer states are not monotone in depth: W̃ ranges over 0.39 to 0.88 and Ũ over 0.01 to 0.37, with L16 lower in source share (0.62) and L24 low in snippet share (0.05). v1 also saw L16's state separate sources less.

Against the references (observed; walk shares). The references contain no model state, so they show what plain token statistics give:

  • Source: the bag of the prefix's tokens reproduces the state's source grouping (W̃ 0.87 against 0.85 for the whole state), and its sets agree with the whole state's at AMI 0.58.
  • Snippet: the bag groups by snippet more strongly than the state (Ũ 0.49 against 0.22); the last-16-tokens reference matches the state (0.20).
  • Class at t: neither reference reproduces the state's grouping (C̃c 0.49 for the whole state, against 0.06 for the bag and 0.08 for the recent reference).
  • Predictive coherence: neither reproduces it either (κ̃ 0.23 against 0.03 and 0.04; κ̃|T 0.12, about B-point's 0.12, against 0.02 and 0.02).

The sets, read from the cards (observed; source make-up in brackets).

  • Set 1 (1,908 items): code and forum together (code 71%, forum 29%), the merged pair of the Overview's diagnosis point 4.
  • Set 2 (591): LaTeX-heavy maths (maths 92%, forum 7%).
  • Set 3 (1,530): wiki (wiki 98%, forum 1%), including runs of Category: lines.
  • Set 4 (1,076): forum questions (forum 86%, code 12%).
  • Set 5 (120 items from only 29 snippets): licence headers in code ("This program is free software ...").
  • Set 6 (148): line ends in verse (class make-up newline 95%, indent 2%; source poetry 99%, wiki 1%), the same kind of context as B-point's set 1.
  • Set 7 (1,113): maths prose (maths 93%, wiki 4%).
  • Set 8 (1,490): verse (poetry 97%, wiki 3%).

The whole state's ψ₁ runs from import lines in code to line ends in verse.

How I read it (reading). The state's leading groupings are mostly by kind of document, and for source a bag of tokens does as well. So on this probe the state's document grouping is not shown to exceed token statistics. The state does carry a token-class and predictive association that the bag and recent references lack, about as large beyond the token as the residual's.

What else it could be.

  • The class association is partly trivial. Each layer's conv buffer holds its last few inputs, so the current token, and with it its class, is in the state by construction.
  • The predictive association does not establish prediction-specific representations, and does not rule out every token-statistics explanation: richer statistics than a bag (order, recency weighting) are not tested.
  • Boilerplate repeated across snippets (licence headers, category lines) makes near-identical prefixes; some sets may partly be that.

4. Along reading, residual sets fade within one or two tokens; the state's sets keep most of their retention past sixteen, except its verse line-end set

Claim (observed; K4 met). The residual's sets: B-point's eight set vectors, followed in the point L16 lag snapshots, have mean retention 0.91 at τ = 0, 0.47 one token later, 0.22 two tokens later and 0.06 after sixteen. At L8 and L24 the mean halves by τ = 2 and τ = 1.

The state's sets: the whole state's eight vectors, in the whole lag snapshots, have mean retention 0.93 at τ = 0 and 0.65 after sixteen tokens.

  • Seven of the eight keep 60% to 95% of their lag-0 value.
  • The exception is the verse line-end set (set 6): vector 6 keeps 8% of its lag-0 value.
  • B-state's vectors in the state L16 lag snapshots behave the same way: vector 5 keeps 16% of its lag-0 value, and the others 63% to 96%. B-state's set 5 is again verse line ends (newline 82%, function word 8%; poetry 99%, forum 1%).

Span agreement says the same: point L16 against itself one token later has a₈ = 0.19, and the whole state against itself sixteen tokens later 0.64. In the residual, what survives the lag is source: in point L16, W̃ is 0.58 at τ = 16, while the lag-0 class share falls from 0.66 to 0.04.

How I read it (reading). This fits findings 1 and 3. Groupings by the token just read, in the residual or in the state's one token-class set, are re-formed with each new token. Groupings by kind of document change slowly.

What else it could be. Anything that integrates the prefix would persist this way: a bag of 16 to 112 tokens changes little when 16 more are added. The run has no lag snapshots of the references, so this does not separate the state's memory from prefix statistics (see the checks below).

5. No object is certified as clustered at the tested numbers of parts: B-point is excluded under the θ rule, the state blocks keep undetermined cases; K5 is not met

Claim (observed). No object, references included, is certified at any number of parts k ∈ R (2 to 32).

  • B-point. The multi-way ratio Υ̂(k) is at most 0.908. The cap 2μk/μk−1, which bounds every partition, is 2.02 to 2.96, below θ = 3 at every k. So under the θ rule certification is excluded at every tested k. That is a statement about reaching a ratio of 3 with k parts, not about the absence of every kind of grouping.
  • B-state is undetermined at k = 2, and the whole state at k = 2, 3 (caps 2.01 to 3.69); undetermined is not evidence of absence. Both are excluded at the other k.
  • B-point with 8 graph neighbours instead of 15 changes one outcome: at k = 2 its cap is 3.01, so that case becomes undetermined (best ratio 0.921). Nothing is certified there, or with 30 neighbours. With either, the sets barely change (AMI with the k = 15 sets 0.89 and 0.86).
  • Zoom trees.
    • T1 (B-point): root Υ = 0.797, and 0 of 7 cuts at or above 3.
    • T2 (whole): root Υ = 1.36; its one clear cut is node 1 (n = 3,170, Υ = 4.54; children by source: wiki 1,536, forum 25 | poetry 1,579, wiki 5), the wiki/verse split v1 also found.
    • T1's first cut separates layout and punctuation contexts (newline, symbol, sentence punct, open; 2063 items) from words (word start, function word, word cont, number; 5937).
    • T2's first cut separates poetry 1,596, wiki 1,541 from code 1,597, maths 1,595, forum 1,575.

The fixture shows that the same pipeline certifies planted clusters at this N (full-size check: planted 1.51e+03, structureless 1.9).

How I read it (reading). These walks do not have gap-separated k-way partitions of the strength θ asks for. For B-point the spectrum rules them out at every tested k, and for the state blocks the question is open at two or three parts. The sets are therefore best read as summaries of leading modes (a rounding of ψ₁..ψ₇), and their boundaries need not be natural cuts.

  • Readouts that carry the result: walk shares, κ̃ and κ̃|T, η² of the modes, retention, span agreement, and AMI read as "what the leading modes separate".
  • Readouts that do not: certification, the number of sets, where set boundaries fall, and the quality of tree splits.

What else it could be. θ is a convention, and only "excluded" is a theorem about the operator. The sample size relative to the graph's degree may matter (see the checks).

6. Compared with the HF random initialisation, training creates the residual's groupings and multiplies the state's source grouping (K6 met)

Claim (observed). Same items, same groupings, init against trained:

  • predictive coherence κ̃ at point L24 is 0.000 at init and 0.26 trained;
  • B-point's shares at init are near zero (class at t 0.02, token 0.01), and its r = 8 sets agree with the class only at AMI 0.02;
  • init and trained B-point sets agree at AMI 0.01;
  • the untrained whole state already has W̃ 0.17 and Ũ 0.15 (trained 0.85 and 0.22).

How I read it (speculation). A randomly initialised recurrence still accumulates token statistics over the prefix, which a bag shows is enough for some document grouping. Training strengthens that grouping several-fold and creates the residual's token-class organisation from almost nothing.

What one run can and cannot support

  • Scope. The findings describe this construction on this probe; none is a claim about Mamba in general, and none enters THEORY.md. The run covers one model and one probe (five sources, two of which the walk merges), one draw of item positions, and one graph degree with two sensitivity values. Token classes come from a regular-expression taxonomy.
  • Targets. Three targets failed (K2, K3, K5) and stay failed. K1 has no null and is read with K1b.
  • Thin margins. The largest Sinkhorn row error is 1.93e-12, against the gate's 2e-12: it passes, narrowly. The pred reference has 1 duplicate pair (distance 2.3e-10; exempt under the SPEC 11 amendment, made after pilot 1 and before any measurement was read) and is not tie-sensitive.
  • Labels. Source and class only validate; model outputs (A, κ, pred) are used for scoring and as a reference, never in a block.

Checks I'd like to run

  1. Lag snapshots of bag and recent, to see whether the state's retention exceeds a prefix statistic's (finding 4).
  2. A vocabulary-matched null for the state: permute source within groups of items with similar bags, as κ̃|T does for tokens. This asks whether the state groups by document beyond vocabulary (finding 3).
  3. An order-aware reference, such as a recency-weighted bag or a small n-gram model's state, to test the state's class and predictive associations against richer token statistics (finding 3).
  4. Remove repeated boilerplate (licence headers, category lines) and rebuild the whole state's sets.
  5. Split the state view into the conv buffer and the SSM state at L16 and L24, to explain the non-monotone layers and the conv buffer's share of the class association.
  6. Report κ̃ and κ̃|T at their peak layer next to L24, and AMI with the next token's class, which tests "predicts alike" more directly than A.
  7. Certification on subsamples of N = 2,000 at the same graph degree, to see whether "excluded" depends on the sample size relative to the degree. The graph-degree sensitivity is already in the data (finding 5).

F7: read the sets directly. Each point is one item (a token context). The controls work as follows:

  • object picks whose sets you see: a block (B-point is the residual across layers, B-state the per-layer states, the whole state, or a lag block), or a reference.
  • colour by paints the points: its sets, a validation label, the snippet, or an eigenfunction ψ.
  • SEBA rank r is the number of sets (8 or 16).
  • eigenfunction ends picks which ψ's extremes are listed at the bottom.

Below the layout, the set cards list what each hard set contains: its commonest tokens at t and t+1, how concentrated it is on one token, its class and source make-up, and example contexts with the item's token marked. Click a point for its context, or a card's header to isolate that set. The eigenfunction ends need no clustering to read. Lag blocks' sets are described with the lag-0 tokens (the card says so).

One figure per line of SPEC section 9, in its order (F7 is the Explorer). Each figure opens with one line saying what it shows, filled from the data; the Findings interpret it. Groupings marked validation (source W, token classes Cc, Cn) are used only to score results; A, κ̃ and κ̃|T use the trained model's outputs. F1 is computed from v1's stored data and is real on every build.

Construction

The construction is inherited from v1 (../mamba_coherent/SPEC.md) and, through it, from the Pythia study; only the items, views, blocks and statistics below are new (SPEC.md is the authority).

  1. Items. For each of the 1,000 v1 snippets, 8 distinct positions t from 16 to 112, drawn with a per-snippet seed; item (i, t) is the prefix [EOT] + tokens 1..t. No two items share the same multiset of their last 16 tokens (label-free de-duplication; 22 redraws). Items are stored in a seeded random order. Lags τ ∈ {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16}: the same item read τ tokens later.
  2. Views. point: the raw residual after block l. state: layer l's recurrent state, the Gram average of its conv buffer c and SSM state z. whole: the Gram average of all 48 constituents. References (never in a block): bag (mean input embedding of tokens 1..t), recent (of tokens t−15..t), pred ($\sqrt{p_t}$, the trained model's next-token distribution).
  3. Operator per snapshot (inherited): cosine on unit-normalised vectors, union kNN graph with k = 15 and floor $10^{-6}$, Sinkhorn balancing, lazy walk $P$.
  4. Blocks. B-point (point, L1..L24, the headline), its thirds, B-state (state, L1..L24), B-lag-whole (whole at every τ), B-lag-point (point L16 at every τ). The block operator is the running mean of its snapshots' operators; its eigenpairs give the eigenfunctions $\psi_k$ and, by SEBA at r ∈ {2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32}, the coherent sets.
  5. Statistics. Excess walk shares against each grouping with exact chance and a 50-permutation band; κ̃ and κ̃|T (pairs from the same snippet excluded); η² of ψ₁..ψ16 against each grouping; AMI and matched Jaccard of the hard sets; span agreement ar between objects; lag retention; zoom trees; and the multi-way ratio $\hat\Upsilon(k) = \mu_k/\hat\rho(k)$ with its cap $2\mu_k/\mu_{k-1}$.

Reading rule for clusters (SPEC 5). $\hat\Upsilon(k)$ uses two label-free roundings (SEBA argmax and k-means on ψ₁..ψk−1) and keeps the larger; any complete partition gives a lower bound on Peng, Sun and Zanetti's $\Upsilon(k)$, and the higher-order Cheeger inequality caps every partition at $2\mu_k/\mu_{k-1}$. Certified: $\hat\Upsilon(k) \ge \theta$. Excluded: cap below θ. Undetermined otherwise; that is not evidence of absence. θ = 3 was fixed on the fixture before the run (fixed) and is a reading convention, not a recovery guarantee.

The measured quantities

$$ \tilde S_G = \frac{S_G - S^0_G}{1 - S^0_G},\qquad S_G = \frac1N \sum_{i \ne j,\ g(i) = g(j)} P_{ij},\qquad \tilde\kappa_{|T} = \frac{\kappa - \kappa^{T}}{1 - \kappa^{T}},\qquad \kappa = \frac{\sum_{i,j\ \text{diff. snippet}} P_{ij}\,\mathrm{BC}(p_i, p_j)}{\sum_{i,j\ \text{diff. snippet}} P_{ij}} $$
where $P$ is a snapshot's (or block's) walk on the $N$ items, $g$ a grouping of the items (token at $t$, token at $t+1$, snippet, the model's top-1 prediction, source, token class), $S^0_G$ the exact chance level, $\mathrm{BC}$ the Bhattacharyya coefficient of the trained model's next-token distributions $p_i, p_j$, and $\kappa^T$ the mean of $\kappa$ when the prediction vectors are permuted within groups of items sharing the token at $t$ (50 permutations). $\tilde S = 0$ is chance, $1$ means the walk never leaves the group.

Controls, calibration and the pilot gate

The statuses are in the verdict box on the Findings tab. Calibration of θ on the fixture (check seeds): planted minimum $\hat\Upsilon$ 382 over 80 planted blocks, structureless maximum 1.89 over 5; P1′ passes. Share of planted cases certified, by planted signal strength s (the size of the planted cluster offset relative to the noise): s = 0.5: 62%; s = 0.75: 100%; s = 1.0: 100%; s = 2.0: 100%. Full-size check (N = 8,000): planted 1.51e+03, structureless 1.9: calibrated at full size. Run checks on this data: largest Sinkhorn row error 1.93e-12; smallest off-diagonal cosine distance 4.0e-05; smallest PN(ψ₁) over blocks 188; worst SEBA label reconstruction (the fraction of items whose stored set label is reproduced from the stored vectors; 1 = all) 0.999 over 666 spectral records.

Hazards

  • K1 has no null. It compares two AMIs; a structureless walk can "meet" it by noise. Read it with K1b and with F4's η² against its band.
  • Token identity explains much. Token classes are functions of the token at t, and the token predicts much of pt, so high C̃c or κ̃ alone means "grouped by current token". Only κ̃|T above its band says more. Items whose token is unique in the probe keep their own prediction in the null (B-point share: 30%).
  • κ is normalised by the walk mass it scores (README deviation 2); the SPEC form is stored as kappa_raw. Block κ is κ of the block's $\bar P$, not a mean of its snapshots' κ.
  • θ is a convention. "Excluded" is a theorem about the operator; "certified" depends on θ; "undetermined" is silence.
  • Layouts are display only (UMAP of ψ₁..ψ₁₆, fixed seed). Distances in the picture are not the method's.
  • Sets are hard SEBA sets on assigned items; unassigned items are grey and excluded from AMI.
  • Source is confounded (code and forum mix; Overview, point 4), so source-based targets (K2) are read with that in mind.

Deviations from SPEC.md (quoted from README.md)

  1. De-duplication compares the multiset of the last 16 tokens, not the sequence. recent (mean embedding of tokens t-15..t) is a function of that multiset, so two items whose windows are permutations of each other (on the real probe, typically (i, t) and (i, t+1) when the token leaving the window equals the one entering) are exact duplicates in a reference cell and the v1 duplicate assertion stops U2. The fixture hit this. A shared sequence is a shared multiset, so this is the stricter reading of "share their last 16 tokens". On the real probe: 22 redraws; no two items share their bag multiset either.
  2. kappa is normalised by the walk mass it scores: kappa = sum_{different snippet} P_ij BC_ij / sum_{different snippet} P_ij, which equals SPEC's (1/N) sum when no same-snippet pair carries walk mass; without it, a walk that stays inside snippets would read as predictively incoherent. The SPEC form is stored as kappa_raw with the mass (mass_diff). The within-token null permutes prediction rows within token groups and keeps the exclusion on the walk pair (i, j), so kappa^T uses the same pairs and normaliser as kappa.
  3. Block statistics are computed on the block's Pbar. Shares on Pbar equal the mean of the cells' (linear in P); kappa is a ratio, so a block's kappa is kappa(Pbar) (K1b reads this), not the mean of its cells' kappa.
  4. Pilot = U1 and U2 on trained, then the gate (SPEC: "U1 and the gate"): the gate's Sinkhorn, duplicate and PN checks are U2 outputs. C1a/C1b run inside U1 trained with v1's code on the 1,000 snippets.
  5. Units added: calib_<seed> (the fixture calibration on Modal CPU; locally it would take about 45 min), diag (a CPU probe of SEBA's cost, below). No U0: U1 copies the probe and asserts its sha256 (v1's U0 established the tokenizer facts on the same file). U1 mounts v1's volume to read act_trained.npy for C3.
  6. The guard reserves per stage, and each (unit, checkpoint) is its own Modal function with its own timeout. v1 reserved every remaining unit at every launch. Here that would be $10.3 at 2x timeouts although the projected study total is $6.1; per stage, the pilot reserves $7.23 and the full run (if the pilot costs as projected) $7.65. The ceiling is still enforced before every dispatch, so nothing can spend past $8; the risk is only that the full run is refused after an expensive pilot.
  7. Groupings and objects: lag cells are scored against T, Cc, U, W (lag 0) and T_tau, without kappa; B-lag-point and B-lag-whole against T, Cc, U, W. recent also gets a spectral object (SPEC lists bag and pred); the references are not computed at init. Set descriptors of lag cells use the lag-0 tokens. The matched-Jaccard null keeps v1's 200-permutation bank; shares, eta^2 and kappa use 50.
  8. Also stored (v1 inheritance): each block's retention of psi_1..8 and of its r = 8 SEBA vectors in its own cells (M-form, v1 block_record), next to the SPEC's lag retention (P-form, chance -1/(N-1)).
  9. eta^2's lambda-weighted mean uses lambda_k(Mbar) (k = 1..16). SEBA at r uses the constant and psi_1..psi_{r-1} (v1 and Froyland's convention), so r = 32 uses the 33rd eigenpair's predecessors only.
  10. Calibration seeding: each block draws from default_rng([seed, k, sizes_index, round(100 s)]) (structureless: [seed, 0, 0, 0]); one structureless block per seed. The SPEC fixes seeds but not how cases derive from them.
  11. Implementation speed-ups that do not change the mathematics: SEBA and k-means for the 9 ranks run concurrently, each single-threaded; UMAP layouts (fixed random_state, single-threaded) run in parallel processes; NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=1 in the image.
  12. The decode was not benchmarked (Stage A spends nothing on the model). The projection takes v1's measured decode (42 s per pass over the 1,000 snippets on an L40S) with a 1.5x margin.
  13. v1's two-way Upsilon in the trees is read against v1's threshold 3.0 (its P1 value); theta for Upsilon_hat(k) is this study's calibration (also 3.0).
